findings.message: _intake_write_result forks a jq subprocess on every terminal exit path including the success path; introduced by this change, though intake is a single-shot non-LLM stage so the added latency (one fork + one atomic write per run) is negligible in practice.

mkdir -p is called unconditionally inside _intake_write_result on every invocation; because multiple failure-path calls can occur within one intake_run (none do today, but the function is public), this results in redundant directory-creation syscalls on each call rather than once at stage init; introduced by this change.

The SPEC-2 SIGTERM sub-test introduces a sleep 0.3 busy-wait before killing the subprocess; combined with the identical sleep 0.3 in the integration SPEC-16 test, this change adds at least 600ms of wall-clock sleep to every CI run; introduced by this change.

The SPEC-9 rewrite now calls intake_run twice in sequence to verify per-run event emission, doubling the in-process intake_run invocations in that section relative to the previous single-call check; introduced by this change, cost is proportional to intake_run overhead per call.
